findings.title: Per-customer OAuth2 authorization code flow
findings.detail: Each customer redirects to Linear's authorization URL, Linear returns a code, and the app exchanges it at the token endpoint for an access token and refresh token. The access token is documented as valid for 24 hours and must be refreshed when it expires.
findings.appliesWhen: Each individual customer account connects through its own OAuth grant.

evidence.quote: When authorizing a user to the Linear API, redirect to an authorization URL with correct parameters and scopes:
### Example ```http GET https://linear.app/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID&redirect_uri=YOUR_REDIRECT_URL&state=SECURE_RANDOM&scope=read HTTP/1.1
`state` | (optional, **recommended**) Prevents CSRF attacks and should always be supplied. Read more about it here.

fields: client_id from the OAuth2 application
redirect_uri matching the registered callback
state: a random value stored by the app for CSRF verification
scope: read (default, required)

steps.title: Exchange the authorization code for an access token
steps.detail: After the callback returns a code whose state matches the stored value, POST the code to the token endpoint as form-encoded data with grant_type=authorization_code, the same redirect_uri, client_id and client_secret. The response contains access_token, refresh_token and expires_in; the access token lasts 24 hours.
steps.doneWhen: The token response contains an access_token with scope including read, and a refresh_token is stored securely.

steps.title: Read the first page of issue titles
steps.detail: Send POST to https://api.linear.app/graphql with Content-Type application/json and Authorization: Bearer ACCESS_TOKEN. Query issues(includeArchived: true, first: 10) { nodes { id title } pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor } }. Read the title scalar from each node in data.issues.nodes. Record data.issues.pageInfo.hasNextPage and data.issues.pageInfo.endCursor. Archived issues are hidden from paginated responses by default, so includeArchived: true is passed. If hasNextPage is true, the next-page step continues with endCursor as after. Boundary check: confirm the request is a read-only query and the request log shows no create, update or delete of issues.
steps.doneWhen: The response has data.issues.nodes with title strings and data.issues.pageInfo with hasNextPage and endCursor. The request log shows only the read query with no issue create, update or delete.

evidence.quote: } ``` To query the next 10, simply pass the value of `pageInfo.endCursor` as `after` parameter for the next request. You can do this as long as `pageInfo.hasNextPage` return true
#### Archived resources Archived resources are hidden by default from the paginated responses. They can be included by passing optional `includeArchived: true` as a query parameter for pagination.
``` Or pass the token as an authorization header: `Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>`

request.example: curl '-X' 'POST' 'https://api.linear.app/graphql' '-H' 'Content-Type: application/json' '-H' 'Authorization: Bearer ACCESS_TOKEN' '--data' '{"query":"query Issues { issues(includeArchived: true, first: 10) { nodes { id title } pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor } } }"}'

fields: ACCESS_TOKEN: OAuth access token from the token exchange for the connected customer account

steps.title: Read the next pages of issue titles using endCursor
steps.detail: While the prior response's pageInfo.hasNextPage is true, send the same read-only query with variables {"after": prior pageInfo.endCursor} and first: 10, including includeArchived: true. Read each page's title scalars from data.issues.nodes. Repeat until data.issues.pageInfo.hasNextPage is false, which is the documented end of the listing. Two pages alone do not complete the listing. Boundary check: confirm the granted scope is read with no issues:create or write scope, and confirm the request log contains only issues queries with no create, update or delete of issues.
steps.doneWhen: Paging stops only when data.issues.pageInfo.hasNextPage is false, after every page of issue titles was read through endCursor. The grant and request log show read-only access with no issue create, update or delete.

evidence.quote: } ``` To query the next 10, simply pass the value of `pageInfo.endCursor` as `after` parameter for the next request. You can do this as long as `pageInfo.hasNextPage` return true
and you'll paginate through all the values in the collection.
* `read` - (Default) Read access for the user's account. This scope will always be present.

request.example: curl '-X' 'POST' 'https://api.linear.app/graphql' '-H' 'Content-Type: application/json' '-H' 'Authorization: Bearer ACCESS_TOKEN' '--data' '{"query":"query Issues($after: String) { issues(includeArchived: true, first: 10, after: $after) { nodes { id title } pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor } } }","variables":{"after":"END_CURSOR_FROM_PREVIOUS_RESPONSE"}}'

fields: END_CURSOR_FROM_PREVIOUS_RESPONSE: pageInfo.endCursor from the prior response
ACCESS_TOKEN: same customer OAuth token used for the first page
